analysis.title: Mirion Technologies - Q3 Quick Take - Margin Miss May Overshadow Growth Outlook
key_insights: Northland expects MIR's Q3 results may be taken negatively. Adj EBITDA of $65 million missed consensus of $69 million, and the 2026 Adj EBITDA guidance was pushed to the low end of the prior range even though revenue guidance was raised.
Q3 revenue of $278 million was slightly above consensus and Northland's estimate of $276 million. Adj EBITDA of $65 million was below consensus of $69 million and Northland's estimate of $67 million.
Q3 Adj EBITDA margin was 23.3% against 23.5% in Q3 2025. It missed management's guidance for higher margins y/y.
2026 total revenue growth guidance was raised from 22%-24% to 24%-25%. Organic revenue growth guidance was raised from 5%-7% to 7%-8%.

2026 Adj EBITDA guidance was narrowed from $285-$300 million to $285-$292 million, versus consensus of $290 million and Northland's estimate of $287 million. Adj EBITDA margin guidance fell from 25%-26% to 24.7%-25.2%.
Implied Q4 Adj EBITDA of about $101-$108 million is slightly better than consensus of $102 million and Northland's estimate of $100 million.

Large orders booked in Q3 were $140 million, up from the $55 million secured at the time of Q2 earnings. MIR targets $125 million in Q4, which would bring the full-year total to $369 million versus the prior full-year opportunity set of $318 million.
Backlog reached a record of about $1.2 billion, up from the prior record of about $1.1 billion in 1H 2026. Organic orders grew 62% y/y to $340 million and total orders grew 85% y/y to $386 million.
Nuclear power end-market organic orders grew 105%, largely driven by the installed base. Northland reads this as showing MIR is more than a bet on newbuilds and SMRs.
MIR repurchased 3.6 million shares in Q3 for $56 million (about $15.56 per share). $235 million remains on the recently refreshed $250 million buyback.

Northland says a fair amount of pessimism is already priced in at 13.7x EV/EBITDA on 2027 versus peers at almost 16x. It expects the update to keep questions about MIR's margins and 2027 expectations alive.

market_movers.rationale: Northland keeps its Outperform rating and $24 target after Q3. Strong orders and record backlog offset the Adj EBITDA miss and the low-end margin guidance, and the shares trade at a discount to peers on 2027 EV/EBITDA.

earnings_insights: MIR Q3 2026 revenue reported at $278 million vs consensus and Northland estimate of $276 million.
MIR Q3 2026 Adj EBITDA reported at $65 million vs consensus of $69 million and Northland estimate of $67 million. Adj EBITDA margin was 23.3% vs 23.5% in Q3 2025.

MIR 2026 guidance: total revenue growth 24%-25% (prior 22%-24%), organic growth 7%-8% (prior 5%-7%), Adj EBITDA $285-$292 million (prior $285-$300 million, consensus est $290 million, Northland est $287 million).

MIR 2026 Adj EBITDA margin guidance is 24.7%-25.2%, down from 25%-26%. Adjusted FCF guidance rose from $155-$175 million to $170-$185 million. Non-GAAP EPS guidance changed from $0.48-$0.55 to $0.50-$0.54.

MIR implied Q4 2026 Adj EBITDA is about $101-$108 million (guidance-derived) vs consensus est $102 million and Northland est $100 million. Q4 is expected to have mid-teens+ organic growth in Nuclear & Safety and mid-single-digits+ in Medical.
MIR booked $140 million in large orders in Q3 (reported) and targets $125 million in Q4, for a full-year total of $369 million versus $318 million at the prior update.
risk_factors: Highly regulated industries: nuclear power, governments and medical. Noncompliance or regulatory changes could hurt performance.
Debt and leverage: debt must be serviced and covenants met, and the debt has claims senior to common shareholders.
Exchange rates: global operations expose results to currency moves against the U.S. dollar reporting currency.
Acquisition risk: MIR has been acquisitive and there is no assurance acquisitions deliver the expected benefits.
Margin risk: the Adj EBITDA miss and the lower margin guidance keep questions about margins and 2027 expectations open.
vol_and_positioning: Shares short are 32,513,654 against 243.3 million shares outstanding and a 96.4% float, per FactSet data in the report.
MIR trades at $15.41, near the low end of its 52-week range of $14.04 to $30.28. Northland says a fair amount of pessimism is already priced in.
MIR trades at 13.7x EV/EBITDA on 2027 versus peers at almost 16x.

tension_points.bull_case: Revenue guidance was raised, backlog hit a record of about $1.2 billion, organic orders grew 62% y/y, and the shares trade at 13.7x 2027 EV/EBITDA versus peers at almost 16x.
tension_points.bear_case: Q3 Adj EBITDA of $65 million missed consensus of $69 million, Q3 margin of 23.3% was below the 23.5% a year earlier, and 2026 Adj EBITDA guidance moved to the low end of the prior range.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further margin pressure that keeps questions on MIR's margins and 2027 expectations unresolved.
